name: Sharmistha Sahoo/ଶର୍ମିଷ୍ଠା ସାହୁ

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Sharmistha Sahoo, also published as Sharmistha Sahu, is an Odia poet associated with Talcher. Her collections include “Rati Jagualira Daka”, published by Black Eagle Books in 2021. In an Odisha Sambad interview, she recalls an early encounter with the writing of Mitrabhanu Gountia and copying songs from her father’s notebook. The account places poetry’s beginnings in listening, reading and the experience of language before a formal literary career.

Her two poems here examine what breaks or falls silent while the surrounding world continues. “Bhangiba Muhurta” moves through wind, forest light, a departing bird and temple sounds before turning towards deliberate violence. “Maa Chup Hoijiba Mane” transforms the repeated demand that a mother be quiet into the irreversible silence of death. Its questions about a surviving voice refuse to let an ordinary household loss disappear into the world’s indifference.
